items.title: Donn Andre interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, June 6, 2009
items.q: we used another fellow who was part of the original Catatonic Five, Derry Hall, who was from Clinton.

ctx.x: In the years you were here, obviously some members graduated and stuff. Was there competition to get into the Catatonic Five?

Yes there was. There were a horn player and a piano player, and they went off to form their own band, and then when we needed a piano player sometimes we used this one fellow. But the other guy on trumpet was not really tuned in that much. In fact, for a couple of years and when we went to Europe and when we went to Carnegie Hall, our piano player and trumpet player were from Colgate. And I don’t know how that happened. I mean we were desperate for a musician, a piano player and a trumpet player, © Fillius Jazz…

in September of whatever year it was that they joined the band. And I guess Emerson knew somebody at Colgate and said, “Gee do you know any guys that play,” and they said, “Yeah there’s these two guys. They’re both pretty good, the piano player is extraordinary, exceptional.” So he went to Europe with us but he couldn’t make the Carnegie Hall gig so we used another fellow who was part of the original Catatonic Five, Derry Hall, who was from Clinton.
